Name: Shannon Tuley
Badge: Everyday Sparks
Which strategy from this module (Writer’s Notebook, Quicklists, or Writing Sprints) feels most immediately usable in your teaching context? Why?:

The quicklist and writing sprints feel most immediately usable in my teaching context for a few reasons. The first is that this is a very low prep activity. The students generate their own writing topics based on their answers to a few questions. This also brings me to another reason this is immediately applicable to my teaching: student buy-in. Students are more likely to meaningfully write when they are writing on topics that are not only relevant to them, but also ones that they choose. This can create interest in writing for the student. This is also something that is most immediately usable because it is the easiest to fit into my daily schedule.

What do you anticipate will be the biggest challenge in bringing daily writing into your classroom, and how might you address it?:

The biggest challenge in bringing daily writing into my classroom might be keeping students writing the entire time. I could also see several students not taking the quicklist seriously enough. I do anticipate more buy-in since students pick their own topics to write about, however, it could still be an issue. I plan to address it buy gradually making the writing sprints longer to build writing stamina.
